mockText: 100 items in 2 hours, with 4 drag-and-drop style items, flags and a review screen. Built for the v2.0 exam that starts February 3, 2027. Cisco doesn't publish the real item count, the real exam can include hands-on labs, and you can't go back once you answer. Practice the same way: answer each one and keep moving.
lead: The classic network engineer cert. It proves you can build, run and secure a small to mid-size network on Cisco gear: switching, routing, IP services, security basics and automation. A new version, v2.0, starts February 3, 2027, with more troubleshooting and an AI domain.

v20.label: v2.0
v20.note: The new blueprint: five domains, more troubleshooting, and a 10% AI and operations domain. Pick this if you'll test on or after February 3, 2027. Same exam number, same CCNA.

Check that the diagram matches what's really connected.
show commands and logs, ping, extended ping, traceroute and packet captures.

extras.title: How a router picks a route
rows: Longest prefix match wins: a /24 beats a /16 for an address in both.
Same prefix from different sources: lowest administrative distance wins.
Same source and prefix: lowest metric wins.
No match at all: use the default route (gateway of last resort), or drop the packet.

method: Pick your version by test date, then use its domains as the checklist.
Learn each protocol well enough to explain it, configure it and spot it broken.
Lab every week: Packet Tracer or Cisco Modeling Labs. Build VLANs, trunks, OSPF, NAT and ACLs from a blank config.
Daily subnetting drills, plus flashcards for AD values, show commands and port numbers.
Timed 120-minute practice exams. Cisco exams don't let you go back, so practice deciding and moving on.
tips: Simulations take longer. Bank time on quick multiple-choice questions and don't overthink them.
You can't go back to earlier questions. Read every word of the exhibit first.
In config labs, verify with show commands and save with copy run start if the task asks for it.
There's no penalty for guessing, so always pick something.

quiz.q: From 172.16.8.0/24 you need as many subnets as possible, each with at least 50 usable hosts. Which mask do you use?
o: Right. A /26 gives 62 usable hosts per subnet and four subnets. It's the smallest block that fits 50.
Enough hosts (126), but only two subnets. Not as many as possible.
Only 30 usable hosts. Too small.
One subnet. It fits the hosts but gives no subnetting at all.

quiz.q: Which IPv6 address type starts with FE80::/10 and is never routed off the local link?
o: Link-local
Right. Every IPv6 interface makes a link-local address. Routers won't forward it, and OSPFv3 uses it for neighbors.
Global unicast
Global unicast (2000::/3) is routable on the internet.
Unique local
Unique local (FC00::/7) is like private IPv4: routable inside an organization.
Multicast
Multicast addresses start with FF00::/8.

quiz.q: A trunk between SW1 and SW2 is up, but SW1 logs a native VLAN mismatch (VLAN 1 on SW1, VLAN 99 on SW2). What's the effect?
o: Untagged frames from VLAN 1 on one side land in VLAN 99 on the other, so the two VLANs leak into each other
Right. Native VLAN traffic is sent untagged, so each switch puts it into its own native VLAN. Match the native VLAN on both ends.
The trunk carries no VLANs at all
The trunk still carries the tagged VLANs. Only untagged traffic is affected.
Spanning tree blocks every port on both switches
STP may block the port for that VLAN, but not every port.
Only the native VLAN works
It's the reverse: the tagged VLANs work and the native one is mixed up.

quiz.q: Which pair of features belongs on an access port for a user's PC, so it comes up fast but shuts down if someone plugs in a switch?
o: PortFast and BPDU guard
Right. PortFast skips listening and learning. BPDU guard err-disables the port if a BPDU arrives, which means a switch was connected.
Root guard and loop guard
Root guard protects the root bridge choice and loop guard catches lost BPDUs. Both are for links between switches.
BPDU filter and PortFast on trunks
BPDU filter can hide real loops, and PortFast doesn't belong on trunks to other switches.
UplinkFast and BackboneFast
Old 802.1D features. Rapid PVST+ builds them in.

quiz.q: A router has 10.0.0.0/8 via OSPF (AD 110), 10.1.0.0/16 as a static route (AD 1), and 10.1.1.0/24 via OSPF (AD 110). Which route does a packet to 10.1.1.50 use?
o: The OSPF route to 10.1.1.0/24
Right. Longest prefix match comes first. AD only breaks ties between routes to the exact same prefix.
The static route to 10.1.0.0/16, because AD 1 is lower
AD matters only for the same prefix. The /24 is more specific.
The 10.0.0.0/8 route
It matches, but it's the least specific of the three.
The default route
The default route is used only when nothing more specific matches.

quiz.q: An engineer adds ip route 192.168.50.0 255.255.255.0 10.0.0.2 200 on a router that already learns 192.168.50.0/24 through OSPF. What happens?
o: The static route stays out of the table and takes over only if the OSPF route disappears
Right. AD 200 is worse than OSPF's 110, so it's a floating static route: a backup.
It replaces the OSPF route, because static always wins
Static routes win only with their default AD of 1. This one was set to 200.
Traffic is load-balanced across both routes
Routes from different sources with different AD values don't load-balance.
The router rejects the command
The command is valid. The number at the end sets the AD.

quiz.q: R1 (10.1.1.1/24) and R2 (10.1.1.2/24) share a link and both run OSPF with matching hello and dead timers. R1 has the link in area 0 and R2 has it in area 1. What happens?
o: No adjacency forms, because the area IDs don't match
Right. Neighbors on a link must agree on the area, subnet, timers and authentication.
They become neighbors, and R2 becomes an ABR
An ABR needs interfaces in two areas. These two interfaces disagree on one link, so they never become neighbors.
They become neighbors, but the DR election fails
They never get far enough to elect a DR.
Different router IDs stop them
Router IDs are supposed to be different. Duplicate IDs are the problem case.

quiz.q: Two hundred inside hosts share one public IPv4 address, and the router tracks them by port number. What is this?
o: PAT (NAT overload)
Right. Port Address Translation maps many inside addresses to one outside address using different source ports.
Static NAT
Static NAT maps one inside address to one outside address.
Dynamic NAT with a pool
A pool maps each inside host to a free outside address, one to one.
NAT64
NAT64 translates between IPv6 and IPv4.

quiz.q: Users can reach www.example.com, but outside mail sent to people at example.com bounces with “no mail server found.” Which DNS record is missing or wrong?
o: MX
Right. Mail servers look up the domain's MX record to find where to deliver.
A
The A record maps a name to an IPv4 address. The website working shows it's fine.
CNAME
A CNAME is an alias for another name.
PTR
PTR is reverse lookup, IP to name. Some mail servers check it, but it doesn't tell them where to deliver.

quiz.q: Hosts in 10.1.1.0/24 must not Telnet to server 10.2.2.10, but everything else should be allowed. Which is correct?
o: access-list 110 deny tcp 10.1.1.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.2.2.10 eq 23, then access-list 110 permit ip any any, applied inbound near the source
Right. An extended ACL can match the port, and it goes close to the source. The permit line keeps the implicit deny from blocking everything else.
access-list 10 deny 10.1.1.0 0.0.0.255, applied near the server
A standard ACL can't match a port, and without a permit it blocks all traffic.
access-list 110 deny tcp 10.1.1.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.2.2.10 eq 23 with no other lines
The implicit deny at the end would block all other traffic too.
access-list 110 deny tcp 10.1.1.0 255.255.255.0 host 10.2.2.10 eq 23, then permit ip any any
ACLs use wildcard masks. 255.255.255.0 as a wildcard matches the wrong addresses.

quiz.q: Someone plugs a home router into an access port, and it starts handing out addresses with a fake default gateway. Which switch feature stops it?
o: DHCP snooping
Right. Only trusted ports (toward the real DHCP server) may send DHCP offers. Offers on untrusted ports are dropped.
Dynamic ARP inspection
DAI stops forged ARP replies. It relies on snooping's table, but doesn't block DHCP offers itself.
Port security
Port security limits MAC addresses per port. It wouldn't know the offers are fake.
Storm control
Storm control limits broadcast floods, not DHCP servers.

quiz.q: An Ansible playbook pushes the same NTP settings to 40 Cisco switches. Which statement is true?
o: Ansible is agentless: it connects over SSH or an API and needs no software on the switches
Right. That's why it fits network devices: nothing to install, just reachability and credentials.
Each switch needs an Ansible agent installed first
That's how Puppet and Chef traditionally work. Ansible doesn't need an agent.
Ansible uses SNMP traps to apply the change
SNMP is for monitoring. Ansible pushes changes over SSH or APIs.
Ansible can only manage Linux servers
It has modules for Cisco IOS, IOS XE, NX-OS and many other platforms.

quiz.q: You plan to paste router configs into a public generative AI tool to summarize what changed. What should you do FIRST?
o: Remove or mask sensitive data such as passwords, keys and internal addresses, based on its classification
Right. Anything sent to a public tool may be stored. Classify and sanitize the data before you pick the format or persona.
Ask for the output as JSON
Output format is a good prompt detail, but it doesn't protect the data.
Give the AI a persona, like senior network engineer
Personas can improve answers. They don't stop secrets from leaking.
Paste the full config so it has all the context
More context with secrets in it is exactly the risk.

quiz.q: Which syslog severity level is the most severe?
o: 0, Emergency
Right. Levels run 0 to 7, and lower numbers are more severe. 0 means the system is unusable.
7, Debugging
Debugging is the least severe and the most verbose.
3, Error
Errors matter, but levels 0 to 2 are worse.
5, Notification
Notifications are normal but significant events, like an interface coming up.

pbqs.title: Subnet the cutter's network
pbqs.scenario: You have 10.40.0.0/24 for four networks. Give the biggest network the first block, then work down, with no overlaps and no wasted space. Pick each network's subnet and mask.

rows.why: 100 hosts need a /25 (126 usable). Biggest first, so it starts at 10.40.0.0 and runs to .127.
50 hosts need a /26 (62 usable). The next free block after .127 is 10.40.0.128, through .191.
20 hosts need a /27 (30 usable). Next free is 10.40.0.192, through .223.
A point-to-point link needs a /30 (2 usable). Next free is 10.40.0.224.

pbqs.title: Diagnose from the output
pbqs.scenario: Each snippet comes from a different trouble ticket. Pick what it shows. Each answer is used once; two choices are distractors.

items.log: %CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH: Native VLAN mismatch discovered on GigabitEthernet0/1 (1), with SW2 GigabitEthernet0/1 (99).
items.why: CDP noticed the two ends of the trunk use different native VLANs. Set the same native VLAN on both.

items.log:
%SPANTREE-2-BLOCK_BPDUGUARD: Received BPDU on port Gi1/0/14 with BPDU Guard enabled. Disabling port.
%PM-4-ERR_DISABLE: bpduguard error detected on Gi1/0/14, putting Gi1/0/14 in err-disable state
items.why: A switch was plugged into a PortFast access port. Remove it, then shutdown and no shutdown the port.

items.log: %OSPF-4-ERRRCV: Received invalid packet: mismatched area ID from backbone area, from 10.1.1.2, GigabitEthernet0/0
items.why: The neighbor's hellos carry a different area ID, so no adjacency forms. Put both interfaces in the same area.

items.log:
R1# ping 172.20.5.1
.....
Success rate is 0 percent (0/5)
R1# show ip route 172.20.5.1
% Network not in table
items.why: The router has no route to that network and no default route. Add a static route or advertise it in OSPF.

items.log:
R1# show access-lists
Extended IP access list 110
    10 deny tcp any host 10.2.2.10 eq 443 (1882 matches)
    20 permit ip any any (90311 matches)
(Ticket: nobody can reach https on 10.2.2.10)
items.why: Line 10 is denying HTTPS to that server, and its match count keeps climbing. Fix or remove the line.

items.log:
Neighbor ID   Pri  State      Dead Time  Address    Interface
2.2.2.2         1  FULL/BDR   00:00:35   10.1.1.2   Gi0/0
items.why: FULL means the databases are synchronized. This neighbor is healthy, and the problem is elsewhere.
